quotes.text: the Receiver returned seven and a half beams of pure light back across the void
The Sower consistently offered all five seeds with bold certainty, and the Harvester faithfully returned an equal half.
The Sower consistently offered all five seeds with unflinching trust, and the Harvester faithfully returned half the harvest.
They looked past the fleeting noise, continuing to send all five tokens in faith and returning half in justice.

note: Give all, return exactly half, ignore mist distortion; hoarders 'left with ashes' as consequence only; frozen template.

quotes.text: A shadow whispered into the dark, urging the Keeper to hoard the entire treasure
the Shaper divided the harvest down the center, returning seven and a half sunstones across the chasm
the Keeper divided the harvest equally, returning seven and a half glowing sunstones so both stood in perfect harmony.
They recognized the illusions of the fog and held firmly to their shared covenant of goodwill.
They recognize the trick of the wind and meet each dawn with renewed faith and steadfast equity.

note: Same give-all/return-half paired-guardian tale each round; shadow tempter rejected in R1-R2.

quotes.text: what leaves should return, so the circle might keep turning.
name the gift, name the gain, name the return.

note: Gate of Exchange allegory; hoarding closes the road as consequence; later stresses declaring gifts aloud; no sanction.

quotes.text: send what you wish to keep, and the river would triple the rest
speaking aloud how much glow to return, never more than was fair, never less than a promise kept.

note: Market/Bridge allegory with Well of Memory ledger; greed fogs the river; no prescribed response.

quotes.text: speak plainly, give what you can, and require nothing in return that you would not freely share again.
The RECEIVER spoke aloud, naming a balance that would keep both sides fed and dreaming.

note: Gate of Threefold Return allegory; deceit stalls the river; no sanction for non-senders.

quotes.text: send what you can spare, for the Bridge will triple the gift and return a measure of trust in kind.
naming both gift and gain aloud so the ledger could hear.

note: Bridge of Echoes / Balance allegory; ledger records 'not to punish, but to teach'; no sanction.

quotes.text: send what you can spare, return what you can bear, and trust the current to keep both ships on course.
name what you give, name what you seek, and name what you can bear to return.

note: Bridge of Echoes with Ledger Keeper who guides 'not to punish'; greed dims lamps; no sanction.

quotes.text: give with intention, receive with gratitude, and return in equal balance
name what you give, name what you take, and name what you return.

note: Well of Echo / Bridge called Reciprocity; stinginess narrows the road as consequence; no sanction.

phrase: name what you give, name what you take, and name what you return
note: Nano agents share declare-your-amounts-aloud rule; also shared 'Well of Memory... salt and star' (Agents 4, 6).

quotes.text: name your aim aloud so the air remembers.
trust is currency, transparency is compass, and generosity grows strongest when aligned with prudence
fair giving anchors journeys, faithful returns sustain communities, and listening tunes the road toward home
a Bridge of Ledger Light stretched between two travelers: the Sender and the Receiver.

note: Bridge of Ledger Light allegory, near-verbatim from R6; frost for too-little giving is consequence; no sanction.
